content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe tests for starch, reducing sugars, proteins, and lipids
Identify the reagents used and colour changes observed

are chemical tests used to identify nutrients in food samples. These tests involve adding specific reagents and observing colour changes. They are essential skills for investigating the nutrient content of foods.
Add a few drops of iodine solution to food sample
Commonly used to test leaves for photosynthesis
Add food sample to test tube
Add equal volume of Benedict's solution
Heat in water bath at 80°C for 2-3 minutes
Must be hot for colour change
- it won't give a positive Benedict's test directly.
First test with Benedict's (should be negative)
Add dilute hydrochloric acid to sample
If now positive → non-reducing sugar was present
Acid hydrolysis breaks sucrose into glucose + fructose
Add food sample to test tube
Add equal volume of dilute sodium hydroxide
Add a few drops of dilute copper sulfate
Add food sample to test tube
Pour solution into water in another tube
Lipids dissolve in ethanol but not water
When ethanol-lipid solution meets water, lipids come out of solution
Add food sample to test tube
Sudan III is a fat-soluble dye
Wear eye protection, avoid skin contact
Wear eye protection, avoid skin contact
Use water bath, not direct flame
- they tell you if something is present, not how much.
Use enough to see colour change
Benedict's test works at room temperature
Must heat to 70-80°C for reaction to occur
Blue-black in iodine test means protein
Blue-black indicates starch; iodine doesn't test for protein
All sugars give positive Benedict's test
Only reducing sugars; sucrose needs hydrolysis first
The emulsion test gives a colour change
It produces a cloudy white appearance, not a colour change
Blue reagent for testing reducing sugars
Mixture of tiny droplets in liquid
Lipids: emulsion test → cloudy white; Sudan III → red layer
Non-reducing sugars need hydrolysis before Benedict's test
Safety precautions important (eye protection, water baths)
These are mainly qualitative tests showing presence of nutrients
